Keywords: discoverability, first use, what can I do, hidden controls, signifier
Description: Two qualities matter most: the user can discover what actions are possible and where (discoverability) and understand what they mean (understanding)
Do: Make every possible action visible or one obvious step away; test on someone who has never seen the screen
Don't: Hide controls behind gestures/long-press/unlabeled icons for elegance
OTL Note: HMI: every function the operator needs during a batch must be visible on the batch screen

Keywords: signifier, affordance, label, sticky note, handwritten sign, button looks clickable
Description: A signifier is a perceivable cue telling WHERE and HOW to act; it matters more than the abstract affordance. A handwritten note taped to a device means the design failed
Do: Make tappable things look tappable (filled block / frame / icon + text); put the cue at the place of action
Don't: Rely on signs or instructions to explain an ambiguous control; flat text that is secretly a button
OTL Note: If a customer or worker writes a note next to an HMI button the button is redesigned not the note

Keywords: low contrast cue, invisible signifier, black on black, subtle hint
Description: A signifier only works if it can be perceived in the real conditions (lighting distance gloves stress)
Do: Check cues at the real viewing distance and lighting; high contrast; large enough
Don't: Black-on-black embossing; 1px hairline as the only cue; hover-only cues on touch screens
OTL Note: Roastery = smoke + glare + 1-2 m distance; verify on the panel not only on the PC

Keywords: mapping, layout, spatial, controls near object, stove burners, switch bank
Description: Map controls to what they control. Best = control on the object; second = right next to it; third = same spatial arrangement
Do: Put the setpoint/button directly on or beside the value/equipment it acts on; arrange controls in the same layout as the machine
Don't: A 1-D row of identical buttons controlling a 2-D arrangement; controls far from their value
OTL Note: Gas/air/drum controls sit next to their live value on the roast screen

Keywords: direction, increase decrease, up down, slider orientation
Description: Vertical position maps to quantity: up = more. Keep increase/decrease directions identical everywhere
Do: Plus/up/right = increase on every screen
Don't: Mixed directions between screens; mirror-image controls

Keywords: culture, next previous, scroll direction, metaphor, time axis
Description: Natural mapping depends on viewpoint and culture (does the top button go next or back? does content or window move?). Switching metaphors causes a period of errors
Do: Pick one metaphor (time flows left to right; content moves with finger) and use it on every screen and product
Don't: Change the metaphor between app web and HMI versions of the same function
OTL Note: Time axis left to right everywhere (roast curve; logs)

Keywords: feedback, latency, 100ms, response, button press, loading
Description: Feedback must be immediate (delay of ~0.1 s already feels broken) and informative. Without feedback people press again (and an even number of presses can cancel the command)
Do: Acknowledge every press within 100 ms (pressed state); for long actions show progress + estimated time (slightly pessimistic)
Don't: Silent buttons; single generic beep/flash that only says something happened
OTL Note: Command buttons on HMI need a visible pressed state even if the PLC/board answer comes later

Keywords: too much feedback, beeps, notification overload, back-seat driver
Description: Too much feedback is worse than too little. Prioritize: unimportant info shown unobtrusively; important info must capture attention
Do: Rank every message/sound by importance and give each tier its own presentation
Don't: Beep on every action; toasts for routine success; repeated reminders
OTL Note: Keep the click sound subtle; reserve loud sound for alarms

Keywords: meaningful feedback, blink codes, beep patterns, error codes
Description: Feedback must say WHAT happened. Blink/beep codes (1 blink = X; 2 blinks = Y) are not remembered
Do: Show the result state in words + value (e.g. 'Gas 45% -> 50%')
Don't: Coded blinks or numeric-only error codes without text
OTL Note: Board status codes must be shown as text on HMI/web/app

Keywords: mental model, how it works, system image, explanation
Description: People build a mental model from what they see (the system image). The UI must suggest a simple correct model; a wrong model (fridge with 2 knobs) makes control impossible
Do: Show how inputs relate to outcomes (e.g. 'Now 75 deg; will be 72 deg in 20 min'); name things by the user's model
Don't: Two controls that look independent but interact; internal implementation names
OTL Note: Show 'ET 230 / target 240 / reaching in ~2 min' style text during preheat

Keywords: what user wants to control, temperature and flow, faucet, physical vs psychological
Description: Let users control the variables they care about (temperature + flow) not the machine's internal variables (hot + cold valves)
Do: Expose goal-level controls (target BT / roast level) and translate internally
Don't: Force users to juggle internal actuators to reach a goal

Keywords: gulf of execution, gulf of evaluation, seven stages, feedforward
Description: Each screen must let the user answer: What do I want? What are the options? What can I do now? How? What happened? What does it mean? Is it OK / goal reached?
Do: Use the 7 questions as a review checklist; feedforward (options) + feedback (results) bridge both gulfs
Don't: Screens that show controls but not the resulting state (or state without the available actions)
OTL Note: Use as the acceptance checklist when reviewing an HMI screen

Keywords: human error, blame user, error message, design error, root cause
Description: There is no 'user error' at scale: if many people make the same mistake it is a design error. Difficulties are signifiers of what to fix
Do: Log and study every repeated user mistake; fix the design; ask 5 Whys past the human
Don't: Blame/retrain the operator; error messages that scold
OTL Note: Customer complaints about wrong presses = redesign input

Keywords: input format, date format, phone format, validation, parse
Description: Accept every reasonable input format and convert it; never reject a format the system could understand
Do: Parse '1:30' '90s' '1m30'; trim spaces; accept comma or dot decimals
Don't: Error 'invalid format' after typing a valid value in another format
OTL Note: Comma/dot decimal for Vietnamese users

Keywords: error message, recovery, start over, guidance
Description: Replace error messages with guidance and let the user fix it from where they are; assume the input is partly correct
Do: Keep entered data; highlight the field; say how to fix
Don't: Clear the form; force restart from step 1

Keywords: memorize, recall, knowledge in the world, menu, visible options
Description: The best way to help memory is to make it unnecessary: put knowledge in the world (visible options; labels; current state). Experts still go fast; novices and returning users can still operate
Do: Show options and current values; label everything; keep reference values on screen
Don't: Require memorized codes/sequences; rely on training for rare procedures
OTL Note: Rare procedures (calibration; cleaning) need on-screen step lists

Keywords: short-term memory, working memory, 3-5 items, interruption
Description: Plan for working memory of only 3-5 items wiped out by any interruption
Do: Keep what the user needs to compare on the same screen; chunk long numbers
Don't: Make users carry numbers from one screen to another; long codes

Keywords: toast disappears, transient message, auto-dismiss critical
Description: Critical information must not disappear just when the user needs it
Do: Keep critical messages until acknowledged and available in a history/log
Don't: Auto-dismiss toasts for errors/alarms; messages that vanish on screen change
OTL Note: Board alarms on web/app stay listed until seen

Keywords: auto logout, session timeout, interruption, lockout
Description: Auto-logout and over-strict security under frequent interruptions makes people write things down or bypass it; too secure becomes less secure
Do: Keep timeouts proportional; preserve state across re-login; never lock a machine in the middle of a process
Don't: Long lockouts; losing work on timeout; complex passwords changed often
OTL Note: OTL rule already: PIN lock 30 s max; never lock while roasting/preheating

Keywords: reminder, notification, prospective memory, due
Description: A reminder needs both the signal (something to do) and the message (what) at the right time and place
Do: Notification text says what to do and appears at the moment it is actionable
Don't: 'Reminder!' with no content; reminders too early or too late
OTL Note: Maintenance reminders on HMI at batch end not mid-roast

Keywords: constraints, physical, cultural, semantic, logical, disable invalid
Description: Use four constraint types to limit possible actions: physical; cultural (conventions); semantic (meaning); logical (only one place left). Make constraints visible before the action
Do: Disable/hide actions that are invalid in the current state; show why
Don't: Let the user try an invalid action and then show an error
OTL Note: Charge button only active when preheat done; show the reason when not

Keywords: make order irrelevant, either way works, symmetric
Description: Best fix for an orientation/order error is making the order irrelevant (battery with identical ends)
Do: Make the system accept actions in any order when the order does not matter
Don't: Impose sequence for implementation convenience

Keywords: activity-centered, device-centered, mode screen, workflow
Description: Group controls by activity (roast; preheat; cooling) not by device (gas screen; motor screen). Manual override must remain and must not cancel the running activity
Do: One screen per activity with all controls it needs; manual adjustments available inside it
Don't: Make the user hop between device screens during a task; manual change that aborts the activity
OTL Note: AUTO + MANUAL on the same roast screen (existing OTL rule)

Keywords: interlock, lock-in, lockout, forcing function, prevent
Description: Forcing functions stop the next step until the previous is done: interlock (correct sequence); lock-in (cannot stop prematurely / exit without save); lockout (blocks entry to danger). Keep nuisance low or people disable them
Do: Use interlocks for dangerous sequences; let the lock-in dialog offer the action directly (Save / Discard / Cancel)
Don't: Forcing functions so annoying they get bypassed; lock-in without a way out
OTL Note: Gas ignition interlocks; exit-without-save prompts in app

Keywords: consistency, convention, standard, change existing UI
Description: Consistency is a virtue: change a convention only if the new way is vastly better and then change it everywhere; mixed systems are worst
Do: Keep one convention across HMI web app; migrate fully when changing
Don't: Partial redesign leaving two styles/behaviours
OTL Note: One button language across HMI/web/app

Keywords: standardize, cannot map, arbitrary, design system
Description: When no natural mapping is possible standardize: same arbitrary rule everywhere so it is learned once. Standards should follow the psychological model not the mechanics
Do: Write the rule into the style guide and apply it to every screen
Don't: Each screen/product inventing its own arbitrary mapping

Keywords: sound, beep, audio feedback, alarm sound, annoyance
Description: Sounds should convey information about the source/action; generic beeps annoy; pleasant sounds become annoying with repetition; silence removes feedback
Do: Short distinct sounds per meaning; volume tiers; user can mute non-critical sounds
Don't: Same beep for everything; long jingles; mandatory sounds for routine actions
OTL Note: Existing OTL metal-click sound must stay subtle

Keywords: capture slip, similar sequence, expert error, procedure
Description: Capture slip: a frequent sequence takes over a rare one when the first steps are identical; happens more to experts
Do: Make rare procedures differ from common ones from the very first step; show reminders on rare paths
Don't: Rare/dangerous flow sharing the first screens with the daily flow
OTL Note: Calibration / factory reset must not start like the normal start sequence

Keywords: similar buttons, identical controls, wrong target, row of switches
Description: Description-similarity slip: right action on the wrong object when controls look alike. Rows of identical controls or meters invite it
Do: Make controls with different purposes differ in shape position color+text; separate dangerous ones physically
Don't: Identical buttons side by side for different equipment (flaps vs gear)
OTL Note: Emergency/stop/drop actions look and sit apart from routine buttons

Keywords: mode error, mode indicator, auto manual, hidden mode, state
Description: Modes give the same control different meanings. Avoid modes; if needed the current mode must be highly visible and different modes must look different (Airbus -3.3 deg vs -3300 ft/min)
Do: Big persistent mode indicator; different value formats per mode; confirm mode in the action label
Don't: A small 'dr' or tiny badge as the only mode cue; same input field meaning two units
OTL Note: AUTO/MANUAL/PC control and degraded modes shown large in the header

Keywords: automation failure, fallback, degraded, sensor lost, offline
Description: Automation fails silently and switches to fallback (GPS -> dead reckoning shown as 'dr') leaving the human out of the loop. Fallback/degraded states must be loud
Do: Banner + color+icon+text when data is stale/simulated/estimated or a sensor is lost; show data age
Don't: Keep displaying last values as if live; tiny fallback indicators
OTL Note: Show 'Mất kết nối' / stale data clearly on web/app; thermocouple fault on HMI

Keywords: interruption, resume, state restore, multitasking
Description: Interruptions are the main cause of memory lapses; the cost includes resuming. Keep goal/step/system state visible so work can resume
Do: Show the current step and what is left; restore position after navigation or reload
Don't: Lose wizard progress on navigation; hide plan/goal after the action starts
OTL Note: Show batch phase + next step on every roast screen

Keywords: sanity check, out of range, unusual value, confirmation threshold
Description: Electronic systems can check whether a request is sensible (1000x dose; won entered as USD)
Do: Validate ranges and compare with the user's usual values; ask only when unusual
Don't: Blindly execute any syntactically valid value
OTL Note: Setpoints outside normal roast ranges ask before applying

Keywords: undo, confirmation dialog, are you sure, destructive, trash
Description: Undo is the most powerful error tool. Confirmation dialogs mostly fail (people focus on the action not the object and click OK) and only catch slips not mistakes
Do: Provide undo/trash; if confirming show the OBJECT prominently and the consequence; make irreversible actions harder
Don't: Routine 'Are you sure?' on every action; dialogs that hide which item is affected
OTL Note: Hold-1s for dangerous commands (existing OTL pattern) + undo where possible

Keywords: segregate controls, dangerous action, hide irrelevant controls
Description: Put easily confused controls far apart; hide controls not relevant to the current operation behind extra effort
Do: Separate destructive actions; show only controls relevant to current phase
Don't: Delete next to Save; all controls always visible

Keywords: alarm flood, too many alarms, nuisance alarm, disable alarm
Description: Warnings are not a solution: many similar beeps sounding together; alarms that report known things get taped over/disabled and forgotten
Do: Rationalize alarms: each must need an operator action; prioritize; coordinate; meaningful and not annoying
Don't: Alarm for every state change; identical alarm tones
Source: Norman DOET ch5 + Hollifield HPHMI p12

Keywords: defense in depth, layers, redundancy, multiple causes
Description: Accidents need many holes aligned. Add layers; shrink holes; alert operators when several holes line up
Do: Combine interlock + clear state + confirmation for critical actions; show when several warnings are active
Don't: Single-point safety relying on one person's attention

Keywords: automation, monitoring, operator in the loop, AI assist
Description: Do not make humans monitor machines for long or act with machine precision; design human+machine as a collaboration (weak human + machine + good process beats either alone)
Do: Machine does precision and vigilance; human decides; keep the human informed of what automation is doing and why
Don't: Leave the human only the hard leftovers; silent automation
OTL Note: AI/PC control must show what it is doing and allow takeover

Keywords: intentionally hard, two-person, safety cover, secure action
Description: When something must be hard (danger; security) make ONLY that step hard; the rest follows good design
Do: Covered/held/two-step actions for danger; normal UX everywhere else
Don't: Making whole screens obscure for 'security'
OTL Note: Factory settings behind PIN; operation screens stay easy

Keywords: complex, complicated, simplify, power users
Description: Complexity is fine when it matches the task; confusion is bad. Tame complexity with a good conceptual model and structure
Do: Keep needed functions; group them with clear structure and naming
Don't: Remove needed functions to look simple; random placement

Keywords: inclusive design, adjustable text size, contrast, aging users
Description: There is no average user; flexible solutions (adjustable size/contrast/brightness) help everyone; large high-contrast text helps all in dim light
Do: Allow text scaling and contrast options; large type for key values
Don't: Fixed small text; designing for the 50th percentile only

Keywords: feature creep, too many features, competitor features
Description: Creeping featurism kills usability; nobody budgets removing features. Strengthen real strengths; be good enough elsewhere
Do: Each new feature must justify its screen space; remove/hide unused ones
Don't: Copy every competitor feature onto the main screen

Keywords: usability test, observe users, five users, iterate, prototype
Description: Requirements come from observing real use not from asking. Test with ~5 real users then fix then 5 more; pairs thinking aloud; record
Do: Observe operators at the machine; quick prototypes; iterate
Don't: Spec written in the abstract; one big test at the end
OTL Note: Watch real roasters use the HMI before calling it done

Keywords: information vs data, context, normal range, raw numbers, operator
Description: 'Information is data in context made useful.' A screen full of numbers forces operators to compare each with a mental map of normal values
Do: Show each key value against its normal/abnormal range (analog indicator; target; trend)
Don't: Pages of raw numbers; P&ID drawing with numbers sprinkled on it
OTL Note: Roast screen shows BT/ET vs profile/target not just numbers

Keywords: gray background, low contrast, glare, dark screen, HMI background
Description: Use a muted gray background to reduce glare; equipment drawn 2D low contrast; color reserved for meaning
Do: Neutral gray/dark-neutral background; low-contrast equipment graphics
Don't: Saturated backgrounds; black background with bright green text
OTL Note: OTL palette (gray/black-matte/red/blue/brown) applies; red only for meaning

Keywords: color meaning, red green status, saturated color, alarm color
Description: Bright/saturated color only draws attention to abnormal situations. Alarm colors (red yellow) are used ONLY for alarms. Inconsistent color use destroys meaning
Do: Normal = neutral; alarm colors reserved; one color table for the product
Don't: Red=stopped/green=running pumps; decorative red; same color meaning two things
OTL Note: OTL red is brand color too: keep it off normal-status items where it could read as alarm

Keywords: color blind, redundant coding, shape plus color, red green
Description: Color alone is never the only differentiator (8% of men color-deficient: red-green; white-cyan; green-yellow). Code redundantly: color + shape + text
Do: Pair every color state with text/icon/shape
Don't: Status shown only by color change of a number or a border
Source: Hollifield HPHMI p10-12; Refactoring UI summary

Keywords: running stopped, on off state, equipment status, brightness
Description: Equipment state = relative brightness + word: brighter than background with 'RUNNING' = on; darker with 'STOPPED' = off; no red/green for normal state
Do: Light fill + word for on; dark fill + word for off
Don't: Green running / red stopped; color-only status
OTL Note: Motor/burner state chips on HMI and web follow this

Keywords: alarm priority, alarm symbol, ISA-18.2, acknowledge, blink
Description: Alarm indication is redundantly coded by PRIORITY (not by type): P1 red square '1'; P2 yellow triangle '2'; P3 orange inverted triangle '3'; P4 diagnostic pink diamond '4'; 'S' suppressed. Symbol beside the value; blinks until acknowledged; stays while condition persists
Do: Distinct symbol + color + number per priority next to the affected value; blink only when unacknowledged
Don't: Only recolor the number/border; code by alarm type; blinking for anything else
OTL Note: Map OTL board alarm codes into 3-4 priorities

Keywords: animation, spinning pump, flame animation, blinking, peripheral vision
Description: No animation except alarm behaviour: the eye notices motion in peripheral vision so motion must mean 'needs attention'
Do: Static graphics; blink only unacknowledged alarms
Don't: Spinning fans/drums; animated flames; moving conveyors
OTL Note: Drum/fan icons do not spin on HMI; web/app micro-motion stays subtle and meaningful

Keywords: trend, embedded trend, history, normal band, sparkline
Description: Most screens should embed 1-2 trends of their key values with history already loaded when the screen opens and show normal band/limits
Do: Embedded trend with dashed limits + light normal band; history on open
Don't: 'One click to trend' (really 10-20 steps; lost on screen change); trends without context
OTL Note: Roast curve always on the roast screen; ET/BT normal band where known

Keywords: analog indicator, gauge, range bar, setpoint marker, normal range
Description: For key values use an analog indicator: gray alarm zones; light-blue desired operating zone; triangle pointer for the current value + number. Scannable in 1-2 s
Do: Range indicator with zones + pointer + number
Don't: Bare numbers; colorful round gauges with decoration

Keywords: bar graph, level, pointer on scale, empty bar
Description: A filling bar disappears at low values (eyes detect presence better than absence). Prefer a pointer/marker moving on a scale; thin level bars with limits over saturated full-width fills
Do: Marker on a scale; narrow level bar + limit marks; trend + analog best
Don't: Saturated full-width tank fill; bar that vanishes near zero

Keywords: exception highlighting, table status, checklist, abnormal row
Description: In tables/lists only abnormal items stand out (bold frame + white background 'NOT OK' / 'MAN'); normal items stay quiet
Do: Exception-based highlighting
Don't: Every row colored; equal emphasis for normal and abnormal
OTL Note: Alarm/event lists: unseen/abnormal rows emphasized

Keywords: display hierarchy, overview, detail, level 1 2 3 4, drill down
Description: Organize screens in 4 levels: L1 overview of whole scope (KPIs; no control); L2 unit control - one screen holds the info + controls for most tasks; L3 detail of one equipment (diagnostics; interlocks); L4 support/diagnostics/procedures
Do: Map every screen to a level; most operation on L2; progressive disclosure downwards
Don't: Flat set of schematic screens ('hard drive with one folder')
OTL Note: Roast screen = L2; settings/calibration = L3/L4

Keywords: navigation bar, persistent nav, main menu, consistent
Description: Same navigation bar in the same place on every screen
Do: Fixed nav with the same items/order on all screens
Don't: Different nav per screen; dead-end screens
OTL Note: OTL dock/nav must be identical across all HMI screens
Source: Hollifield HPHMI p19; Refactoring UI summary

Keywords: shutdown button, emergency, stop, command button, interlock table
Description: Critical commands (SHUTDOWN / FREEZE / ISOLATE) get large distinct buttons; interlock status shown as a table Initiator / Value / Action / Status
Do: Large distinctive shape for critical commands + interlock status table
Don't: Critical command as a small ordinary button
OTL Note: Stop/drop/emergency actions look different from routine buttons

Keywords: schematic, diagram, P&ID, subway map, topology
Description: Draw process/network schematics as topology (subway-map: horizontal/vertical/45 deg lines; only what the task needs) not realistic drawings; avoid crossing lines and inconsistent flow direction
Do: Simplified flow left-to-right; minimal crossings; only task-relevant elements
Don't: Photo-real 3D equipment taking 90% of screen; detailed pipes colored by substance
OTL Note: Machine overview diagram stays schematic and flat

Keywords: 3D, skeuomorphic, gradient, flashy, realistic equipment
Description: Flashy 3D screens spend 90% of area on drawings and 10% on data. Use flat 2D low-contrast graphics
Do: Flat 2D graphics; data gets the space
Don't: 3D tanks with gradients; realistic photos of equipment as background
OTL Note: Matches OTL flat brand (no gradient/shadow)

Keywords: style guide, philosophy, task analysis, HMI project steps
Description: HMI work follows 7 steps: (1) written philosophy + style guide; (2) gap assessment of current screens; (3) operating goals for all modes written down; (4) task analysis -> L2/L3/L4 content; (5) design per guide; (6) install + test + train; (7) maintain + re-evaluate. Follow principles not the (often violating) examples in standards
Do: Keep a style guide file and score screens against it before redesign
Don't: Redesign screen by screen without a guide; copy examples blindly
OTL Note: OTL HMI v28 plan follows these steps

Keywords: design system, style guide, tokens, consistent buttons, type scale
Description: Consistent visual language via a written style guide/design system: fixed primary/secondary button styles; fixed heading/body sizes; same nav on every page
Do: Tokens for color/type/spacing used everywhere
Don't: Per-screen ad-hoc colors/sizes

Keywords: whitespace, spacing, alignment, grid, hierarchy, secondary text
Description: Whitespace is an active element; align to a grid; build hierarchy with size/weight/color/position; secondary info smaller and lighter
Do: Generous padding; grid alignment; de-emphasize secondary items
Don't: Cramming; misaligned blocks; everything same weight
OTL Note: On dense HMI keep spacing scale but tighter; hierarchy by size/weight

Keywords: limited palette, base colors, shades, neutral background, accent
Description: Start from few base colors and derive shades; neutral light background lets accents stand out; color shows state and primary vs secondary action; test colors on several screens and lighting
Do: Small palette + generated shades; neutral backgrounds
Don't: Many unrelated hues; color as decoration
OTL Note: OTL palette wins over any suggested palette; the summary's 'subtle shadow/gradient for depth' is REJECTED for OTL (flat brand)

Keywords: dashboard, key metrics first, drill down, overload
Description: Dashboards show the most important information first and let users dig deeper; do not overload with features
Do: Primary KPI block on top; details on demand
Don't: All metrics at equal size; feature-stuffed home screen

Keywords: accent stripe, accent bar, colored edge, border-top, border-left, top bar on button, underline, card stripe, edge highlight, decorative bar
Description: OTL owner ban (11/10/2026 - "cực ghét, cấm tuyệt đối"): no colored accent stripe or bar attached to the edge of a button or card (top bar; bottom underline; left stripe) anywhere in the product
Do: Separate button groups with whole-tile fill + icon/text color + spacing and a divider between groups; show ON/active state with whole-tile fill inversion plus a state word (CHẠY / ĐANG MỞ)
Don't: Red 4px bar on top of command buttons; colored underline under the active tab; border-left 4-6px accent on cards; inset-shadow stripes
OTL Note: Owner standard overrides any skill/book suggestion of accent borders. Existing in product (scan 11/10): HMI ui_dock.py (ON = red top bar; active = red underline); ui_tai_khoan.py brand panel right-edge bar; Roast Lab .nsfav/.profcard border-left

Keywords: active nav, selected tab, current screen, active state, underline, highlight
Description: OTL owner override of nav-state-active: the current screen/tab is shown by inverting the whole tile (filled background + contrasting text) not by an underline or edge bar
Do: Whole-tile fill for the active item; keep text/icon contrast >= 4.5:1
Don't: Underline or edge bar as the only active indicator
OTL Note: Applies to HMI dock; web rails/nav; app tabs
